transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?

...My lieutenant sent me. I was at the station, just... moving the airway bags around. I had to put them in a pattern. I knew it was the right one. 

I was just repeating the dispatch numbers out loud, and... he told me to stop. To step away. But I wouldn't. I couldn't do that. If I broke the sequence... the whole bay would go bad. So they made me come here.
What did you worry would happen if you weren't able to complete the pattern?

I... I told you. It would just go bad. The whole bay. 

If I didn't finish it... if the bags weren't right with the numbers... things just wouldn't be safe. I don't really know how else to explain it. I just knew I couldn't stop.
Do you ever hear voices that other people around you can't hear?
No. I... no. Just the dispatch. I don't hear anything else.
Did this need to arrange the bags start after a specific call or incident at work?

It wasn't a specific call... well, not exactly. It was... I got hurt. 

About eight months ago, we were doing a transfer, and I messed up my shoulder and my ribs. It just... started after that.
Do you have unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the incident where you injured your shoulder and ribs?
No. I... no. I don't have dreams about it or anything. It was just a physical injury. That's all.
Do you ever feel like an outside force or someone else is controlling your thoughts or actions?
No. I... no. I don't know what you mean by that. Nobody is controlling me. It's just... it's just me.
Deep down, does a part of you feel that arranging the bags might not actually prevent something bad from happening, or are you completely convinced that it will?
I... I don't really know. I don't think about it like that. I just... I just do it because it has to be done. That's all.
